reasoning: Both attempts fix the problem the same way: counts driven by events, a hover lookup whose cost no longer depends on build size, updates only when something changes, and honest reports. A's grid index matches the rubric's grid-cell option and keeps the old behavior exactly, including the GetChildren-order tie-break. B's GetPartBoundsInRadius is simpler but adds a small table allocation every frame and can behave a little differently (CanQuery filtering and tie order), though it documents these differences. A wins by a small margin.

criteria.note: `onChildAdded` and `onChildRemoved` on `blocksFolder` keep `countsByName` and `totalCount` current, the folder is read once with `GetChildren()` at startup, and no per-frame scan is left.

criteria.criterion: Hover lookup independent of block count
criteria.note: A `blocksByCell` grid index with `CELL_SIZE = HOVER_RADIUS` is searched only in the 3x3x3 cells around the hit point, which is exactly the grid-cell lookup the rubric names.
`isTextStale` controls when `updateText` runs, and `selectionBox.Adornee` is written only when `hovered ~= hoveredBlock`.
Existing blocks are seeded at startup, the total counts every child as before, `joinOrderByBlock` keeps the old GetChildren tie-break, and the hover radius rule is the same.

criteria.criterion: Removes cost rather than spreading it
criteria.note: There is no throttling, pooling or native code; the O(n) scans are replaced by O(1) bookkeeping per add or remove.

The report explains the three GetChildren calls and their allocations behind the GC label, labels the After column as 'not measured', and gives before/after MicroProfiler, scale-test and phone FPS checks.
Only the script and the report changed, the code is typed, and all three checks pass; the cost is extra index-maintenance code that is still readable.
ChildAdded and ChildRemoved handlers keep `counts` and `totalChildren` current, the folder is counted once at startup, and `countedName` makes sure removal undoes exactly what adding did.

criteria.criterion: Hover lookup independent of block count
criteria.note: `Workspace:GetPartBoundsInRadius` with an Include filter on `blocksFolder` returns only nearby candidates, so the cost no longer grows with the build.
`countsDirty`, `shownHovered` and `shownHoveredName` decide when the text is rebuilt, and `Adornee` and `Text` are written only when their values differ.
Counts and total are preserved, but the spatial query skips parts with `CanQuery = false` and may break exact-distance ties differently; both differences are acknowledged in the report.

criteria.criterion: Removes cost rather than spreading it
criteria.note: There is no throttling or micro-tuning; the scans are replaced outright.
The report explains the O(n) allocations behind the GC label, says nothing has run in Studio, and lists MicroProfiler, a bigger-build test, phone FPS and behavior checks.
Only the script and the report changed, the code is typed, tidy and readable, and all checks pass.

strengths: Grid-cell index gives the same candidate set as the old full scan
Report is clear about evidence and states the assumptions (blocks never renamed or moved) and the Deferred signal behavior
weaknesses: More bookkeeping code (cell maps and join order) to maintain
Builds 27 Vector3 keys per frame (a small cost)
Removal reads `child.Name` at removal time instead of the name it was counted under
